hooks.prompt: A redirect-hot-path file changed: $ARGUMENTS. Read the changed file (tool_input.file_path) and run `git diff -- <that path>` to see what actually changed. Then read README.md's 'Requirements verified' table and 'Known limitations' tables. If the diff changed something those sections state as true today (a status code, a timeout/threshold, a covered-or-not claim, a documented behavior) — edit ONLY the specific affected line(s) in README.md, minimally and factually, using nothing you have not verified by reading the code. If the diff is cosmetic (rename, comment, formatting, refactor with identical behavior) or you are not confident it changed a documented claim, do nothing and exit without editing any file. If the change looks like it violates one of CLAUDE.md's non-negotiable invariants (e.g. #2 redirect must stay 302 with no-store, #4 uniqueness must come from a DB constraint not a pre-check, #8 writes are never auto-retried) rather than legitimately evolving a documented guarantee, treat that as a likely bug in the code, not grounds to update the doc — do nothing to README.md in that case. Never edit any file other than README.md. Never claim human sign-off (R2) happened or change sign-off wording — that is only ever recorded by a human in docs/ai-traceability-log.md.
hooks.statusMessage: Checking if README.md needs a redirect-path update...
